title: An Agent Said 'Success.' Nothing Happened.
hook: An agent said success. The canonical journal shows nothing happened.
thesis: Agent output is a proposal, not truth. PING's position is that an LLM saying 'success' is not evidence that anything happened; only the canonical journal, written by the one authorized writer and verified by independent observation, counts as evidence. The episode walks the separation between a model claim and a canonical recording, and why that separation is the product's real trust story.

proven: The directive states AGENT OUTPUT != CANONICAL TRUTH as the architectural position (section 4).
The directive states the separation 'the model reasons, the runtime authorizes, the adapter executes, independent observation verifies' (section 9).
partial: That this separation is wired into the runtime's verification and evidence paths rather than stated only in prose.
unknown: The concrete incident receipts, commits, and fixtures to cite publicly. Whether any public example names a real past failure.

approval_gate: Nolan approves every exact post. Silence is not approval.
